newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down in light trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybeans end mostly down in light trade.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mostly down in light volume on Monday with most investors having lost interest in trading after long-term market sluggishness, traders said.
The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 3,250 yuan ($392), up 52 yuan. It opened at 3,195 yuan and hit a low of 3,188 yuan per tonne.
November lost 12 yuan to 3,155, the January 1998 contract 58 to 3,102 and March 10 to 3,140 per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 21,900 tonnes from 23,200 tonnes.
"Speculative buying in the September contract emerged late in the session pushed it up," said one trader.
"But most investors remain sidelined on a lack of market-moving news," he said.
Traders said they expected the market to remain slow in the near future unless some solid stimulating measures were taken.
